rows.text: Yawgmoth turns every creature you own into a card. Pay 1 life and sacrifice another creature: draw, and put a -1/-1 counter where it hurts. The deck is built out of creatures that come back when they die, so that loop never runs out of fodder, and out of drain effects that make every death cost the table life. Grind with it all game; when the right three cards line up, it loops until everyone else is dead. Every loop here takes three cards, so this stays a Bracket 3 deck.

rows.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician
rows.text: four mana, protection from Humans. Pay 1 life, sacrifice another creature: put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card. {B}{B}, discard a card: proliferate.

The -1/-1 counter is how undying and persist creatures loop. A +1/+1 counter and a -1/-1 counter on the same creature cancel, so aiming Yawgmoth at a creature that came back with a +1/+1 counter resets it to come back again.
The draw is not optional. Count your library before a long loop: drain fast enough that the table dies before you deck yourself.
Proliferate adds -1/-1 counters to their creatures (with Nest of Scarabs, Insects for you too) and grows Hancock.

rows.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician + Butcher Ghoul + Geralf's Messenger
rows.text: sacrifice the Ghoul and put the counter on the Messenger; the Ghoul returns with a +1/+1 counter. Then sacrifice the Messenger and put the counter on the Ghoul, cancelling its counter; the Messenger returns and drains an opponent for 2. Repeat: 1 life and one card per step, 2 damage every other step. Any two undying creatures loop; the Messenger is the one that also kills.

rows.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician + Butcher Ghoul + Sightless Ghoul
rows.text: the same loop with no damage built in. Add Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat or Vengeful Bloodwitch and every step drains.

rows.name: Forsaken Miner + Phyrexian Altar + Blood Artist
rows.text: sacrifice the Miner for {B}. Blood Artist's trigger targets an opponent, which is a crime, so the Miner's trigger lets you pay that {B} to return it. Unlimited deaths and drains. Vengeful Bloodwitch or Susurian Voidborn work in place of Blood Artist, and Warren Soultrader in place of the Altar.

rows.name: Nether Traitor + Phyrexian Altar + Pawn of Ulamog
rows.text: sacrifice the Traitor for {B}; Pawn makes a Spawn. Sacrifice the Spawn for another mana, and the Traitor's trigger brings it back for {B}. One mana of profit and two deaths per loop. Add any drain card and it wins.

rows.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician + Nest of Scarabs + Blood Artist
rows.text: every -1/-1 counter you place makes an Insect, and every Insect is more fodder. Not unlimited, but it usually drains the table out.

rows.name: Blood Artist
rows.text: whenever any creature dies, a player loses 1 and you gain 1. The gain pays Yawgmoth's life cost.

rows.name: Zulaport Cutthroat
rows.text: each opponent loses 1 whenever one of your creatures dies.

rows.name: Vengeful Bloodwitch
rows.text: the same as Blood Artist, for your creatures.

rows.name: Susurian Voidborn
rows.text: the same, and artifacts dying count too.

rows.name: Bastion of Remembrance
rows.text: a Zulaport on an enchantment.

rows.name: Syr Konrad, the Grim
rows.text: 1 damage to each opponent whenever any creature dies or a creature card enters or leaves a graveyard.

rows.name: Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER
rows.text: another drain on every death, and it draws when you sacrifice to it.

rows.name: Geralf's Messenger
rows.text: 2 life every time it enters.

rows.name: Grave Pact
rows.text: every creature you sacrifice makes each opponent sacrifice one too. With Yawgmoth, their board disappears.

rows.name: Butcher Ghoul
rows.text: undying, for two mana.

rows.text: undying.

rows.text: undying, and it pumps.

guide.title: Tutor lines — what to fetch, and when

rows.name: Demonic Tutor -> Phyrexian Altar
rows.text: any card. The Altar when you already have Forsaken Miner or Nether Traitor and a drain card; otherwise the missing undying creature.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent -> Geralf's Messenger
rows.text: sacrifice a creature (feeding a drain on the way) for any card.

rows.name: Entomb -> Bridge from Below
rows.text: Bridge does its work from the graveyard, so putting it there IS casting it.

rows.name: Entomb -> Geralf's Messenger
rows.text: then Reanimate, Animate Dead or Unearth it back for an immediate 2-point drain.

rows.name: Unmarked Grave -> Forsaken Miner
rows.text: the Miner only needs to be in your graveyard; the next crime returns it.

rows.name: Unearth -> Butcher Ghoul
rows.text: returns a creature with mana value 3 or less, and cycles when there is nothing to get.

rows.name: Dark Ritual
rows.text: {B}{B}{B} for {B}.

rows.name: Cabal Ritual
rows.text: {B}{B}{B}, or five with seven cards in your graveyard.

rows.name: Songs of the Damned
rows.text: {B} for every creature card in your graveyard, often six or more.

rows.name: Priest of Gix
rows.text: enters with {B}{B}{B}: a free body.

rows.name: Jet Medallion
rows.text: black spells cost {1} less.

rows.name: Sol Ring
rows.text: the usual.

rows.name: Arcane Signet
rows.text: the usual.

rows.name: Lotus Petal
rows.text: free.

rows.name: Mox Opal
rows.text: live with three artifacts: the zero-drops make that easy.

rows.name: Mox Amber
rows.text: taps for black once Yawgmoth or another legend is out.

rows.name: Springleaf Drum
rows.text: taps a summoning-sick creature for mana.

rows.name: Cabal Coffers
rows.text: {B} for each Swamp. Urborg makes every land a Swamp.

rows.name: Lake of the Dead
rows.text: a land that sacrifices a Swamp for four black.

rows.name: Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx
rows.text: black mana equal to your devotion.

rows.name: City of Traitors
rows.text: two mana from one land until you play another.

rows.name: Urza's Saga
rows.text: fetches Sol Ring, Mox Opal, Mox Amber, Lotus Petal or a zero-drop creature at chapter III.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep mana, two or three fodder creatures, and a drain or draw engine. Yawgmoth on turn three or four with fodder ready draws three or four cards on the spot.
Do not loop without a drain on the battlefield: Yawgmoth's draws are mandatory, and drawing twenty cards with nothing dying on their side only costs you life and library.
Before a big loop, count: life you can pay, cards left in your library, and how much each step drains. Stop the moment the table is dead.
